_intent: Shared verification harness for Momentum-managed projects. The 'defaults' block is the all-surfaces-skip posture — a deliberate carve-out for markdown/bash-only repos (like this one) that have no application to run. Skipping every surface is CORRECT for such repos and is not a silent verification gap. A real product repo (one with an app, API, or scripts to execute) MUST add an entry to the 'projects' array to activate real runners for the surfaces that apply. Leaving every surface skipped in a product repo is a silent gap — the 'projects' array is where that is fixed.
_surface_rekey_note: Re-keyed 2026-08 (DEC-040 D7, amending DEC-029): 'execution_surfaces' is keyed by assembled-surface token (verification-standard.md §1) — chat-ui, application-ui, http-endpoint, cli, skill-invocation, hook-trigger, artifact — not by change_type. The legacy change_type-keyed 10-slug scheme (including the unconditional 'backend' -> curl mapping) is superseded; change_type now only supplies an inference fallback when a story declares no surface. 'driver_bindings' also appears at the document root (mirroring 'defaults.driver_bindings' verbatim) as an additive fix for a schema-location mismatch surfaced by this sprint's frozen verification contract, which reads driver_bindings at the root — see the story's cross_artifact_notes. The nested defaults.driver_bindings copy is unchanged and remains authoritative for existing consumers (e2e-validator, qa-reviewer); the two copies must be kept identical.

defaults._note: All-surfaces-skip is the intentional carve-out for a project with no executable surface (e.g. a markdown-only or bash-utility repo). A product repo must override via the 'projects' array below.

platform_matrix.notes: Project verification-harness.json may override to declare specific platforms (android, ios, web, desktop)

trivial_smoke_escape.notes: Set enabled=true and list change_types to bypass smoke validation for trivial stories of those types. Unchanged by the surface re-key — this remains a change_type-keyed escape hatch, distinct from routing.

project._template_note: The block below is a TEMPLATE showing how a real product project configures this harness. Copy it, replace 'example-product-app' with your project slug, and fill in the env values for your stack. Remove this _template_note key before activating.
project.description: Example: a product repo with a chat and application UI, a REST backend consumed directly by external clients, and shell scripts/CLI tools — all runnable surface types configured with real drivers.

env._note: Startup commands and readiness probes apply to surfaces that require a running environment (e.g. chat-ui/application-ui need the frontend, http-endpoint needs the API server). The 'cli' surface runs via cmux bash and does not require service readiness — leave its probe absent. The 'npm run dev &' backgrounding below is intentional; readiness for HTTP services is enforced solely by the curl --retry probes.

execution_surfaces._note: Project entries may use either string values (matching a driver_bindings key — e.g. 'bash', 'curl', 'smoke') or object values for surfaces that need driver-specific options (driver, fallback, scenario_path, base_url_env, platform). The e2e-validator reads the 'driver' key from an object entry the same way it reads a string entry — both resolve to a driver_bindings entry. Surfaces not listed here inherit the shared default (skip). Setting a surface to 'skip' is valid only if the project has no stories declaring (or inferring) that surface.

application-ui.description: UI smoke tests via Maestro for mobile targets; Playwright for web-only flows. Maps to the 'smoke' driver_binding.

chat-ui.description: Drives a conversational surface end-to-end (e.g. a chat UI or agent conversation) via Maestro/Playwright rather than the raw API behind it. Maps to the 'smoke' driver_binding — never 'curl', even when the diff behind the chat surface is backend-only.

http-endpoint.description: HTTP endpoint verification via curl — used ONLY when the endpoint itself is the surface its consumer meets directly (e.g. a public API with no UI in front of it), never as a default for all backend work. Maps to the 'curl' driver_binding.

cli.description: Run CLI scripts/tools in a cmux terminal surface and assert exit code + stdout pattern. Maps to the 'bash' driver_binding.
